topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture topic and outlines the expected learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their mechanisms, toxicities, and drug resistance issues.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular and genetic vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic strategies tailored to exploit specific vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address targeted therapies directed at oncogenic kinases, exploring small-molecule design, resistance pathways, bypass signaling, and clinical limitations.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates selectively target cancer-specific surface antigens to deliver cytotoxic effects.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapy approaches
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the evidence for immune surveillance and examine modern immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint blockade, BiTEs, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Perspectives, historical outcomes, and ethical dilemmas in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate overall progress in cancer care, discussing genomic stratification, prevention versus treatment, historical survival trends, and emerging ethical dilemmas.
